highlightAliases.old: Mean survival ~10y, disability progressing ~10%/yr (p983).
highlightAliases.new: In postmortem-confirmed DLB cases, mean survival ~10y, disability progressing ~10%/yr (p983).

highlightAliases.old: Predictors: older age at motor onset, bradykinesia/non-tremor phenotype, bilateral onset, declining levodopa response, depression, hallucinations (p985).
highlightAliases.new: Possible predictors: older age at motor onset, bradykinesia/non-tremor phenotype, bilateral onset, declining levodopa response, depression, hallucinations (p985).

highlightAliases.old: Orthostatic dx criterion: ≥30 mmHg systolic BP drop (practically, ≥20 systolic/≥10 diastolic considered significant in the absence of an appropriate heart-rate increase) (p986).
highlightAliases.new: In the 2022 MDS criteria, neurogenic orthostatic hypotension is a systolic fall ≥20 mm Hg, usually accompanied by a diastolic fall ≥10 mm Hg, with a blunted heart-rate response. The time window is 3 minutes for clinically established MSA and up to 10 minutes for clinically probable MSA. The 30-mm Hg systolic threshold on p986 reflects earlier criteria.

highlightAliases.old: bvFTD accounts for >50% of FTD cases; pathology ~50% tau, ~50% TDP-43, <10% FUS (p987).
highlightAliases.new: In most centers, bvFTD accounts for >50% of FTD cases; pathology ~50% tau, ~50% TDP-43, <10% FUS (p987).

highlightAliases.old: PPA = isolated language deficit ≥2 years before other decline (p987). nfvPPA: apraxic/agrammatic speech, preserved single-word comprehension; left-dominant atrophy (inferior frontal/insula/caudate); ~20% TDP-43 (type A) at autopsy, remainder tau (CBD > PSP > Pick) (p988). svPPA: fluent but semantically empty speech, surface dyslexia; begins in amygdala/anterior temporal lobe; most behaviorally prominent PPA; usually TDP-43 type C, tau-negative (p988). Logopenic PPA = usually an AD language presentation; may respond to cholinesterase inhibitors (p987).
highlightAliases.new: Primary progressive aphasia: insidious, progressive language impairment is the dominant early deficit and the main initial limitation on daily activities. The book describes an older two-year isolated-language criterion (p987). The international consensus criteria do not require waiting two years to diagnose PPA. nfvPPA: apraxic/agrammatic speech, preserved single-word comprehension; left-dominant atrophy (inferior frontal/insula/caudate); ~20% TDP pathology (usually TDP-43 type A) at autopsy, most show tau (CBD > PSP > Pick) (p988). svPPA: fluent but semantically empty speech, surface dyslexia; begins in amygdala/anterior temporal lobe; most behaviorally prominent PPA; often TDP-43 type C-positive, tau-negative inclusions at autopsy (p988). Logopenic PPA = usually an AD language presentation; may respond to cholinesterase inhibitors if imaging or other biomarkers confirm AD etiology (p987-988).

highlightAliases.old: Treatment: symptomatic only — SSRIs for behavioral symptoms/cravings/compulsions; atypical neuroleptics only if delusions are problematic; no role for cholinesterase inhibitors (may worsen agitation) (p991).
highlightAliases.new: Treatment: symptomatic only — SSRIs for behavioral symptoms/cravings/compulsions; atypical neuroleptics can be considered if delusions are problematic; no theoretical basis for cholinesterase inhibitors (may worsen agitation) (p991).

highlightAliases.old: Incidence 1–2/100,000/yr; ~5,000 new US cases/yr; ~2:1 M:F (p991).
highlightAliases.new: Incidence 1–2/100,000/yr; ~5,000 new cases/yr; ~2:1 M:F (p991).

highlightAliases.old: Symptomatic treatment only; levodopa helps a minority; no role for cholinesterase inhibitors (p992).

highlightAliases.old: Falls as the first symptom in 60%; downward vertical gaze palsy is more specific than upward (mild vertical gaze limitation is normal with aging), with preserved oculocephalic reflex (p992).
highlightAliases.new: Falls as the first symptom in 60%; downward vertical gaze palsy is more specific than upward (mild vertical gaze limitation is normal with aging), with oculocephalic reflex preserved early in disease (p992).

highlightAliases.old: Cholinesterase inhibitors — first-line for DLB (often better response than AD, esp. hallucinations); no role in bvFTD/CBD, may worsen agitation (p984, p991–992).
highlightAliases.new: Cholinesterase inhibitors — first-line for DLB (often better response than AD, esp. hallucinations); no theoretical basis for use in bvFTD/CBD, may worsen agitation (p984, p991–992).

highlightAliases.old: Levodopa — helps parkinsonism in DLB (only after hallucinations/fluctuation are controlled), ~1/3 of MSA patients, and some PSP/CBD patients, but efficacy is limited/wanes (p984, p986, p992).
highlightAliases.new: Levodopa — can be used if indicated for parkinsonism in DLB (once hallucinations/fluctuation are controlled), ~1/3 of MSA patients, and some PSP/CBD patients, but efficacy is limited/wanes (p984, p986, p992).

highlightAliases.new: Possible bvFTD needs 3 of 6 core symptoms (early disinhibition, apathy, loss of sympathy/empathy, repetitive motor behaviors, hyperorality, frontal executive deficit with relative visuospatial sparing) (p982).

highlightAliases.new: DLB can be diagnosed when dementia precedes parkinsonism, begins concurrently, or appears within one year of motor onset. PDD describes dementia after more than one year of established motor PD. The timing convention is described by the DLB Consortium (p984, 2017 consensus).
